Resolves #20064

🌿 A head that earned its green keeps it: the run that lost to a body edit no longer gets to say red.

`File Size Guard` loses its concurrency group, so a body edit no longer cancels the in-flight sibling run on the same head (the 6 of the measured 8). A new `Same-Head Check Repair` workflow listens for `PR Baseline` and `File Size Guard` completions and, when the completed run passed on an open PR, re-runs once every red run of that workflow on the same head whose run number is lower than the witness's: re-runs replace the conclusion in place and both jobs read the live pull request, so the stale red judges the corrected body and goes green (the 2, and the guard's own fail-fix-pass flow). Two files: −3/+2 in the guard, one new workflow (77 lines).

Evidence: L2 (the committed repair script evaluated against a mocked GitHub; both YAML files parsed; the five workflow-parsing unit specs green) and L4 for AC-1 (the arm ran on this PR's own head in hosted CI) → L4 required (AC-4: the repair's first live run, which can only happen once the workflow exists on `dev`). Residual: AC-4, Residual-Owner: #20022.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `js-yaml`: `file-size-guard.yml` has no `concurrency` key. Live arm on this head: the second body version, 20 s after the PR opened, fired `check-size` a second time while the first run was in flight; both runs ended `success` at attempt 1 and the rollup carries two `check-size` `SUCCESS` entries and no `CANCELLED` (first PR comment, 14:26Z). |
| AC-2 | Harness below: witness 20 with `[A failure@1, C cancelled@2, D in_progress, N30 newer failure@1]` → `reRunWorkflowFailedJobs` for A only; with C at attempt 1 → A failed-jobs and C whole-run; the ordering control: an old green (20) completing after a newer failure (30) re-runs nothing, a later green (40) re-runs 30 once; PR closed → nothing. The `if` guard (`conclusion == 'success' && event == 'pull_request'`) is the parsed job condition. |
| AC-3 | Harness below: every API call throwing → one `core.warning` ("Repair skipped: API down"), no `setFailed`. |
| AC-4 | Post-merge only: see Post-Merge Validation. |

## Deltas from ticket
Review round 1 (Euclid, RA-1): "earlier" is now enforced as a per-workflow run-number bound (`earlier.run_number >= run.run_number` skips), with the ordering control in the harness; the first head compared only identity, status, conclusion and attempt, so an old green finishing late could have spent a newer red run's one retry. Fact corrected in place (header comment and `#20064`'s Fix / AC-2): the repair's own check run sits on the `dev` commit a `workflow_run` event runs from, not on the PR head; the never-fail rule stands for that reason. Otherwise none: the repair covers `cancelled` and `timed_out` runs with a whole-run re-run and `failure` runs with a failed-jobs re-run; the ticket named both.

## Test Evidence
Repair harness: the committed `github-script` block of `same-head-check-repair.yml`, parsed out of the YAML and run as an async function against mocked `pulls.get`, `paginate(listWorkflowRuns)`, `reRunWorkflowFailedJobs`, `reRunWorkflow` and a recording `core`; ids are run ids, the numbers after `W`/`N` are per-workflow run numbers, the witness is the run whose completion fired the event.

```
if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request' }}
on.workflow_run: {"workflows":["PR Baseline","File Size Guard"],"types":["completed"]} permissions: {"actions":"write","pull-requests":"read"}
[witness 20: A failure@1, C cancelled@2, D in_progress, N30 newer failure@1] reRunFailedJobs=[1]  reRunWorkflow=[]  setFailed=0 warnings=0 info=1
[witness 20, C cancelled@1]                                                  reRunFailedJobs=[1]  reRunWorkflow=[3] setFailed=0 warnings=0 info=2
[old green 20 completing after newer failure 30 (ordering control)]           reRunFailedJobs=[]   reRunWorkflow=[]  setFailed=0 warnings=0 info=0
[later green 40 after failure 30]                                             reRunFailedJobs=[30] reRunWorkflow=[]  setFailed=0 warnings=0 info=1
[PR closed]                                                                   reRunFailedJobs=[]   reRunWorkflow=[]  setFailed=0 warnings=0 info=1
[every API call throws]                                                       reRunFailedJobs=[]   reRunWorkflow=[]  setFailed=0 warnings=1 "Repair skipped: API down" info=0
```

Mechanism, live, before the change (14:11Z, PR #20063 head a949c64086): its `check-size` run 39965984915 had been cancelled by the body-edit run; `gh run rerun` → attempt 2 `success` at 14:12:39Z → the head's rollup went from `FAILURE` to `SUCCESS` (63 green, 1 skipped), the cancelled entry gone. That is the in-place replacement the repair relies on.

Unit: the five specs that parse `.github/workflows` (`WorkflowScopeClassifier`, `check-guard-ci-parity`, `ScanSurfaceAlignment`, `checkFileSizes`, `buildDependencyResolution`): 113 passed at both heads. The pre-commit `check-guard-ci-parity` hook passed on the staged files.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline `pr-body` / `substrate-size` run in CI.

- **Expected Solution Shape:** Preserve both body-edit triggers and lint semantics; stop cancelling sibling guard runs, then repair only an eligible predecessor of a later successful run for the same workflow/head. - **Patch Verdict:** The placement and cancellation deletion match. At `f545fb883d7267e326cc0df7e2176c2914b3f481`, the new loop checks self/status/conclusion/attempt, but never checks that the candidate predates the green trigger.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** At [the selection guard](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/f545fb883d7267e326cc0df7e2176c2914b3f481/.github/workflows/same-head-check-repair.yml#L59), an older green run that finishes late can select a newer failed run on the same SHA. With the current attempt bound, that premature attempt can leave the newer run permanently ineligible when a genuinely later corrected run passes.

The exact committed-script probe reproduces: trigger20 success + newer30 failure@1 → rerun30; if the body is still bad,30 becomes failure@2; corrected40 success → no repair. The reproduction's creation timestamps make30 newer than20. This is a selection error, not a demand for unbounded retries.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit (per guide §7.4):** “Earlier … after a later run passed” is the intended contract but is not enforced. Separately, the header's claim that the repair's own check sits on the PR head is inaccurate: `workflow_run` uses the default-branch SHA and requires default-branch installation; this repository's default branch is `dev`. That comment can be polished with the behavioral fix. [GitHub event documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_run).

**Findings:** One introduced ordering defect, RA-1.

---

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

- **[RETROSPECTIVE]**: A success completion is not necessarily a later success. An asynchronous repair needs an ordering relation between the witness run and each candidate.
